http_semantics.note: The observed 200 carries a genuine success envelope (operation_id, status completed) of a no-op operation — there is no error remapped into 2xx. Under the documented spec the body is schema-valid (keys present as an empty array; no minItems documented), so the request is not a client error at all per the doc; only under the script's stricter undocumented oracle (empty keys must be rejected) would it count as a client error silently 200-acknowledged. For reference, genuine client errors on this endpoint DO surface as HTTP 400 (missing field keys / invalid type / Either list of point ids or filter must be provided — probes B, C and sibling log 006).

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: only the listed payload keys are removed; unlisted keys persist
contract_grounding.note: The observed no-op satisfies the cited assertion vacuously: zero keys listed -> zero keys removed -> all (unlisted) payload keys persist, readback deep-equal baseline. Per the violates-declaration self-check this is the wrong-constraint-cited branch: the Type1 claim requires an input-requiredness/cardinality norm ('keys must be non-empty' / 'empty keys must yield 4xx') that this constraint never states — its domain is removal selectivity, not request validation. The dispatch's constraint_id field was empty; the id was recovered from the script header (constraint_ids: qdrant_state_payload_delete_001) and does exist in the contract. The only spec-level requiredness on record is raw_knowledge's 'keys: array[string], required: true' (presence), which the observed request satisfies.

chain_trace.break_detail: The chain is mechanically intact (constraint exists, doc reachable, script body matches log echo, log verdict follows the script's oracle), but the DEFECT verdict is unanchored at the doc link: the claim's premise 'the spec licenses no such request (keys required / selector anyOf)' draws from keys Required a cardinality rule the page never states (Required = presence; no minItems) and imports a selector anyOf requirement the page does not state for this endpoint (points and filter are both Optional here, unlike payload+set). The cited constraint adds no support either (different domain: removal selectivity). Live probes confirm the API enforces exactly what the doc marks: keys presence (400 missing field), keys type (400 invalid type), selector presence (400 Either list of point ids or filter must be provided) — and licenses what the doc licenses: empty keys (200 no-op). Whether accepting a vacuous destructive body is a defect is therefore a judgment call on an undocumented boundary, not a violation of a documented promise; chain-auditor to adjudicate.
